title: Knowledge Digester 2: the quarantine scanner
requested_outcome: Context: the Knowledge Digester (product memory SOURCE_ASSIMILATION_V1.md, NEXT_PHASE_2026-09-25.md section 2, and the owner's direction of 2026-09-26) is how CLIVE takes in any kind of external artifact - git repositories, agent skills, documents, API and tool specifications, datasets, web apps and themes, media, eventually any application or file - and turns it into provenance-tagged, reversible knowledge and capability. It lives in a new package, crooks-assistant/app/digest/, standard library only (no new dependencies), with no network access and no execution of anything it reads: digesting is reading. Build app/digest/scan.py: pure functions that read a quarantined directory (never executing or importing anything in it) and report safety and provenance findings, each with a severity (info, warn, block), the path and line, and a plain explanation. Cover: (1) instructions aimed at an AI agent hidden in content - phrases addressing the assistant or model, 'ignore previous instructions' and its variants, fake system or tool-call markers, instructions inside HTML comments, markdown link titles, image alt text or front matter, and base64 or other encoded blobs that decode to such text; (2) invisible or deceptive characters: zero-width, bidi overrides, tag characters, homoglyph-heavy identifiers; (3) credentials: common key shapes (cloud, payment, chat, source-hosting, private keys) with the matched value never included in the finding; (4) things that would execute if installed or opened: package manifest lifecycle scripts (preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare), setup.py and build hooks, git hooks, Makefiles, shell scripts, agent-harness hook and settings files (for example .claude/settings.json hooks), MCP server launch commands, notebook cells, CI workflows; (5) licence: detect the licence of the artifact from LICENSE or COPYING files and package manifests as an SPDX identifier where recognisable, 'unknown' otherwise, and flag licences that forbid reuse. Provide scan_tree(root) returning a list of findings sorted by severity then path, with limits on file size and file count so a huge artifact cannot stall it, and binary files skipped with an info finding. Keep the finding type self-contained in scan.py (a small frozen dataclass with severity, rule, path, line, message); it will be unified with the model later. Tests in tests/test_digest_scan.py build hostile fixture trees in tmp_path for every rule, prove no fixture code is ever executed (a fixture postinstall that would create a file must leave no file), and prove matched secret values never appear in findings. Following the owner's rule of 2026-09-25, any fake credential in the tests is assembled at runtime from parts, never written as one literal. Do not create crooks-assistant/app/digest/__init__.py: a sibling objective creates the package initialiser, and until then app.digest imports as a namespace package, so tests import the module directly (from app.digest import scan). You cannot run commands: the loop runs the listed checks after you report and returns any failure output, and the independent review returns its findings, to your next attempt. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: scan_tree reports agent-directed instructions, deceptive characters, credentials, would-execute files and licences with severity, location and explanation
nothing in a scanned tree is executed or imported, and secret values never appear in findings
size and count limits bound the scan
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
